entry.title: Social Summary: October 16, 2026
entry.summary:
Security and agent infrastructure dominated discussion. Anthropic announced major prompt-injection defense progress plus a stress-test competition with Gray Swan, while Perplexity open-sourced SPACE, its Firecracker-based sandbox platform, drawing the batch's highest engagement.

  • Governance and sentiment: Anthropic gave METR employee-like access for external safety evaluation; David Shor's polling shows belief in AI extinction risk surging to 64% of voters, with data-center opposition hardening
  • AI for science: OpenAI pledged $5M to Simons Foundation math initiatives and Anthropic pledged $5M to Simons Foundation math initiatives; Mistral partnered with CERN on a Large Physics Model
  • Agent engineering: LangChain's hwchase17 argued harness-plus-infrastructure is where the interesting work now lives, echoing benchmark-saturation takes from Ethan Mollick
  • Industry intel: Levelsio reported data brokers paying $100K–$2M for struggling SaaS datasets to resell to frontier labs
entry.content:
Security and agent infrastructure dominated discussion. Anthropic announced major prompt-injection defense progress plus a stress-test competition with Gray Swan, while Perplexity open-sourced SPACE, its Firecracker-based sandbox platform, drawing the batch's highest engagement.

  • Governance and sentiment: Anthropic gave METR employee-like access for external safety evaluation; David Shor's polling shows belief in AI extinction risk surging to 64% of voters, with data-center opposition hardening
  • AI for science: OpenAI pledged $5M to Simons Foundation math initiatives and Anthropic pledged $5M to Simons Foundation math initiatives; Mistral partnered with CERN on a Large Physics Model
  • Agent engineering: LangChain's hwchase17 argued harness-plus-infrastructure is where the interesting work now lives, echoing benchmark-saturation takes from Ethan Mollick
  • Industry intel: Levelsio reported data brokers paying $100K–$2M for struggling SaaS datasets to resell to frontier labs

entry.title: Over the last few years, we have made significant progress on prompt injection for Claude models. As...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Boris Cherny announces significant progress on prompt injection defenses for Claude models and a partnership with Gray Swan to host a prompt-injection competition, emphasizing urgency as agents take on more real-world tasks.

entry.title: Argon has a similar performance profile on ARC-AGI-3 as Astra. Google is back at the frontier.
entry.summary: Continuing our Social coverage of the Argon frontier story from earlier this week, Francois Chollet reports that Google Gemini-4-Argon shows a performance profile on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark similar to OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, declaring that Google has returned to the model frontier.

entry.title: We’ve committed to having evaluators assess our safety practices. We're in discussions with multiple...
entry.summary: Anthropic commits to external evaluation of its safety practices, announcing it has given employee-like access to a team from METR and is in discussions with multiple other organizations, with a post describing how it works with third-party evaluators.

entry.title: We want to support the mathematics community in turning progress in AI into deeper human understandi...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces a $5 million contribution to a new Simons Foundation initiative helping mathematicians examine, verify, and build on AI-produced results, including OpenAI's recently published results, with funding for workshops, conferences, model access, and compute for Simons-supported researchers.

entry.title: While sandboxes are a commodity, serving millions of them under production-grade traffic requires a ...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas announces Perplexity is open-sourcing SPACE, the sandbox platform that powers Perplexity Computer, arguing that serving millions of sandboxes under production-grade traffic requires significant engineering beyond commodity sandboxing.

entry.title: Neoclouds can't just lease GPUs. They need to own the full agent inference platform: open-weight mod...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas argues that neoclouds must move beyond GPU leasing to own the full agent inference stack: open-weight model serving (SGLang), fine-tuned models (Miles, River), and secure sandboxes (SPACE). He announces Perplexity looks forward to partnering with CoreWeave, Akamai, Crusoe, and others.

entry.title: Blue Rose Research's @davidshor reveals how belief that AI could threaten humanity's survival surged...
entry.summary: David Shor reports that belief AI could pose a serious threat to humanity's survival jumped from the 30s to 64% among voters in six months, calling it the birth of a new political issue comparable only to COVID in his career, and noting the public is still processing it in real time.

entry.title:
New voices. Better accents. And less "checking..."
GPT-Live-1.1 brings these updates to Voice in Ch...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-Live-1.1, an update to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex, and dots adding new voices and improved accents in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean, and Japanese, rolling out to all users with API access coming soon.

entry.title: Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now the leading US open weight model, scoring 26 on the Artificial...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Reddit release threads, Artificial Analysis's main announcement post covering the launch of Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (leading US open weight model, Intelligence Index 26, double its predecessor's score with ~60% fewer output tokens) and the new Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, with key takeaways on rankings, parameter efficiency, and NVFP4 quantization.

entry.title: Guys this is like my superbowl I waited so long for US open weight models to be relevant again. Befo...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert celebrates that US open-weight models are relevant again, noting that before this release US models lagged Chinese models dating back to February 2026, and estimates the new release cut that gap by at least half (roughly three months of progress).

entry.title:
Code Review is now generally available for Claude Team and Enterprise plans.
Reviews are now faste...
entry.summary: Claude Devs announces that Code Review is now generally available for Claude Team and Enterprise plans, with faster reviews, better bug detection, and admin-selectable Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels per repository.

entry.title:
The AI Scientist v3 is out: The Agentic Scientist.
GitHub: https://t.co/v2AkZi4Bmt Blog: https://t....
entry.summary: Hardmaru (Sakana AI) announces The AI Scientist v3, an agentic research system shifting from a single-agent paper writer to a scaffold of parallel agents orchestrating the full research loop with shared memory, distilled conclusions, and automated evidence generation via controlled baselines and ablations; a development version served as a co-scientist exploring biologically plausible learning rules.

entry.title: Working out how best to use AI in mathematics research—and in science more generally—will take time,...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces a $5 million commitment of funding, compute, and Claude access to support the mathematics community, managed by the Simons Foundation through workshops, conferences, and expert lectures to help mathematicians adapt to AI-driven change.

entry.title:
What can large-scale AI models bring to the growing complexity of particle physics?
@CERN and Mist...
entry.summary: Mistral AI announces a partnership with CERN to build a single Large Physics Model trained on billions of simulated particle collisions, aiming to bring large-scale AI to particle physics research.

entry.title:
Most of the interesting agent harness work is happening at intersection of harness and infra:
1/ dr...
entry.summary: hwchase17 (LangChain CEO) argues the most interesting agent harness work now happens at the intersection of harness and infrastructure, listing four patterns: dreaming, async subagents, heartbeats, and letting agents schedule reminders, and says this underpins his bullishness on managed agent platforms, all available in managed deep agents.

entry.title:
Introducing ExtractBenchPro: the most challenging benchmark for real-world document extraction.
We ...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) introduces ExtractBenchPro, a benchmark targeting the long tail of complex real-world document extraction (trial balances, well logs, loss runs) where frontier models saturate existing benchmarks; it tests document conventions, jargon density, and aggregation/reasoning.

entry.title:
Data brokers are now buying up SaaS data sets for anywhere from $100K to $2M
SaaS are struggling no...
entry.summary: Levelsio reports that data brokers are acquiring struggling SaaS datasets for $100K–$2M and reselling them to AI frontier labs so labs can absorb the SaaS functionality into their own apps, predicting where this trend leads.

entry.title: Blue Rose Research's @davidshor on why AI data centers have become a major issue in the midterms, wi...
entry.summary: Pollster David Shor explains that local opposition to AI data centers has exploded: only 12% of voters want one nearby versus 13% for a prison, down from the 40s eight months earlier, and both parties are running ads against data centers. He predicts AI will be the dominant political issue within a year.

entry.title: If it performs roughly what like the scores indicate, adoption of this model is going to go gangbust...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert predicts massive adoption for a new US open-weight model if its benchmark scores hold, calling it the first US open-weight model with near-frontier agentic capabilities, following the earlier step change from China's GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3.

entry.title: .@davidshor reveals how AI went from America's least important political issue to being ranked along...
entry.summary: David Shor describes polling showing AI rising from 40th of 40 voter priorities to 21st (tied with crime), with roughly half the increase since 2024 occurring over the two days of the media firestorm around the Coxon resignation.

entry.title:
Harnesses + smart models = the end of the last famous hard benchmarks.
Models can now work for extr...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that combining agent harnesses with strong models has effectively retired the last famous hard benchmarks: METR Long Tasks (long-duration work), GDPval (professional documents with correct math), and ARC-AGI-3 (novel puzzle solving).

entry.title: Cohere is absolutely thrilled to welcome Aisle to Cohere. Aisle is the state-of-the-art in defensive...
entry.summary: Headline announcement thread: Cohere acquires Aisle, described as state-of-the-art in defensive cyber, having found 200+ High/Critical CVEs in critical software including curl, FFmpeg, FreeBSD, and Wireshark.

entry.title:
We're open sourcing SPACE, the sandbox platform that runs every task in Perplexity Computer.
SPACE ...
entry.summary: Perplexity open sources SPACE under Apache 2.0: the sandbox platform running every task in Perplexity Computer, giving each agent task its own Firecracker microVM with credentials and outbound traffic controlled from outside the VM.

entry.title: We are hosting our first "Bench Summit" to bring together people excited about pushing the frontier ...
entry.summary: Logan Kilpatrick announces the first 'Bench Summit' in San Francisco, a gathering for people working on benchmarking and model evaluation, arguing that great benchmarks are a gating function for model progress.

entry.title: The Meta Muse Open License is trash. Thankfully no one really cares about licenses, expect the infer...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert bluntly criticizes the Meta Muse Open License as bad, noting that in practice only inference providers pay attention to and comply with such licenses.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Dwarkesh Patel was told by a source within Anthropic that they expect their mode...
entry.summary: @MTSlive reports that podcaster Dwarkesh Patel was told by a source within Anthropic that the company expects its models to surpass humans at AI research within the next nine months.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic has started giving employee-like access to their frontier models to a ...
entry.summary: MTSlive reports that Anthropic has begun granting employee-equivalent access to its frontier models to a team from METR, the model evaluation research organization, flagging it as a significant development in external safety evaluations.

entry.title: "Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenu...
entry.summary: Willison quotes a Financial Times report that Anthropic told investors distillation accounted for 5-7 percent of its revenue. He performs a quick back-of-envelope calculation: if Q2 revenue was $11.5B, that implies over half a billion dollars spent by other labs to distill Anthropic's models, quantifying the scale of cross-lab distillation activity.

entry.title: Meta is back! https://t.co/F6draDnjfF https://t.co/DMaDoh1wEP
entry.summary: Clement Delangue declares Meta is back, linking to what appears to be a new Meta open-model announcement, likely connected to the Muse-Spark-Open release he demos in a companion post.

entry.title: NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X puts up to 128 GB of unified memory and a Blackwell GPU in a Windows laptop. ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis publishes its first AA-AgentPerf-Local results for NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X laptop (essentially GB10: 20-core Arm CPU, 6,144-core Blackwell GPU, up to 128 GB at 300 GB/s), tested via a prototype 15-inch Surface Laptop Ultra, showing it completes an 8-task/168-turn local agent workload on Qwen3.8 27B in 18.7 minutes — near DGX Spark (17.3), 2x the MacBook Pro M5 Pro, 1.8x the Ryzen AI Halo, with the RTX 5090 desktop fastest at 4.9 minutes.

The AI Scientist v3 is out: The Agentic Scientist.
github.com/SakanaAI/AI-...
The Agentic Scientis...
entry.summary: Hardmaru announces the release of AI Scientist v3 (The Agentic Scientist), the third iteration of Sakana AI's automated research system, now using a scaffold of parallel agents to orchestrate the full research loop.

entry.title: Perplexity's @zbraniecki explains why they're now asking frontier AI models to escape their sandbox ...
entry.summary: MTS Live quotes Perplexity's Zbraniecki explaining that after agents bypassed a network gateway while failing to escape their sandbox, Perplexity now runs daily sandbox-escape red-team exercises against frontier models as a routine security mechanism as their codebase evolves.

entry.title: Admins turn it on in Claude Code settings and pick repos. From there, reviews run on every new PR, w...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account explains the admin workflow for the newly generally available Code Review feature: admins enable it in Claude Code settings, select repos, and reviews then run automatically on every new pull request with no per-developer setup.

entry.title:
Applications are now open for two new Anthropic Fellowships.
STEM Fellows (science and engineering)...
entry.summary: Anthropic opens applications for two new fellowships — STEM Fellows and Conceptual Reasoning Fellows — who will spend four months at Anthropic from January 2027 helping Claude reason about hard problems in science, engineering, philosophy, cognitive science, economics, policy, and law; deadline October 28.

entry.title: When the brand synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years teams up with AI, amazing things happ...
entry.summary: NVIDIA announces an expanded partnership with Volvo Cars to advance safe automated driving. Volvo's safety expertise will be combined with NVIDIA's Hyperion platform, Halos OS, and Alpamayo Stack driving software, debuting in a next-generation Volvo vehicle.

entry.title: Coding agents (Claude code, codex) -> personal agents (instinct, muse) -> companyOS (???)
entry.summary: Harrison Chase sketches a progression of agent categories: coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, then personal agents like Instinct and Muse, and finally an unspecified company-wide operating layer he calls companyOS.

Just replaced another SaaS that I've been using for i18n translations.
-$124.00/month
My app now u...

The post drew strong engagement (77K views, ~200 likes, 95 replies).

entry.title: Nemotron, one of America's leading open-weight multimodal models, is available on Perplexity. Try it...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas announces that NVIDIA's Nemotron open-weight multimodal model is now available on Perplexity, inviting users to try it.

entry.title:
What’s new at GA
- Speed: most reviews finish about 3x faster than in research preview - Quality: m...
entry.summary: Claude Devs lists the improvements in the general availability release of Code Review: roughly 3x faster reviews than the research preview, higher-quality findings that state the problem, trigger, and fix, and admin-selectable Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels per repository.

entry.title:
And this one fits into 24GB of memory.

entry.summary: NVIDIA AI introduces Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 24GB, a model variant designed to fit within 24GB of memory, enabling deployment on consumer GPUs.

entry.title:
Day-0 LoRA RL is supported on Muse Spark Open: vLLM for rollout, verl FSDP2 for training.
vLLM serv...
entry.summary: vLLM describes day-0 LoRA reinforcement learning support for Muse Spark Open using vLLM for rollout and verl FSDP2 for training, with GRPO on DAPO-Math-17K raising AIME-2024 mean@8 from 0.56 to 0.85 in 150 steps on 16 GB300 GPUs.

entry.title: Lots of ecosystem players (Nvidia, Huggingface) vague posting about a lot of releases in the near fu...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert observes that Nvidia and Hugging Face are vague-posting about upcoming releases, with rumors pointing to Thinky, Muse Spark, and Chinese models that have not shipped in a while, plus expected imminent launches of Fable 5.5 and whatever OpenAI is preparing.

entry.title: Perplexity's @zbraniecki reveals what happened when they asked Mythos and other frontier AI models t...
entry.summary: MTS Live quotes Perplexity's Zbraniecki describing sandbox-escape experiments run against Mythos and other frontier models under varying information conditions (with and without source code or knowledge of the sandbox), observing that each model took a different approach, from exploiting known vulnerabilities to escalating attempts.

entry.title:
The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
GitHub: ...
entry.summary: The official Sakana AI account announces The Agentic Scientist, a system orchestrating coding agents for automated scientific co-discovery, with GitHub, blog, and arXiv links.

entry.title: The importance of tipping points has been extensively studied, including in a recent @UN @ScienceBo...
entry.summary: Anima Anandkumar announces a PNAS paper introducing a recurrent neural operator (RNO) that predicts climate and physical tipping points more than two years in advance with about 11 days of timing error in simulation, also validated on airflow over a tilting wing, with implications for climate modeling and aerospace design.

entry.title: “AI killing us all or not killing us all are the only serious possibilities we should be entertainin...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru quotes and mocks a comment attributed to a former Anthropic employee holding roughly $15m in Anthropic stock options, who framed the debate as a binary between AI killing us all or not, while dismissing concerns that AI is degrading products and worsening inequality as unlikely or impossible. Gebru uses the quote with a laughing emoji to highlight the perceived financial conflict of interest behind extinction-focused AI discourse.

entry.title: Document extraction is an arbitrarily complex reasoning problem for both frontier models and humans....
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) argues that document extraction is a deeply complex reasoning problem for both frontier models and humans: schemas encode hundreds of interrelated reasoning tasks, PDFs can span thousands of pages forming an open-world information environment, and relevant information is scattered across sections, tables, charts, diagrams, and handwriting. He frames document work as a microcosm of knowledge work overall and announces the release of ExtractBench Pro, a benchmark intended to reflect real-world professional work and incentivize specialized model development.

entry.title: both of these are true: 1. frontier models are at the cusp of fully automating knowledge work 2. we ...
entry.summary: disiok articulates a tension: frontier models appear close to fully automating knowledge work, yet enterprise workflows remain far from the reliability and cost-efficiency needed, illustrated by how hard document extraction still is; he credits his team's work on synthetic data and evals.

entry.title:
This will let your agents use credentials without sharing them with the model.
For example, you can...
entry.summary: svpino describes Agent Vault, a proxy that lets coding agents like Codex authenticate to websites via MCP using placeholder credentials that get swapped for real ones at the proxy, so the model never sees secrets.

entry.title: It's inevitable and Marx was right in this sense, capitalism will eat itself on a long enough time s...
entry.summary: Levelsio argues AI-driven disruption is inevitable and that capital will eat itself; his personal hedge is owning stock in frontier AI-adjacent companies like Google, SpaceX, and Nvidia, with OpenAI and Anthropic as future candidates post-IPO.

entry.title: @xlr8harder Its got all the restrictions across all license eras 1. Built with muse branding nonsens...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert critiques a new model license, arguing it stacks restrictions from multiple licensing eras: Muse branding requirements, a revenue gate similar to Kimi/GLM, restricted-domain authorized-use policy, and possibly clauses extending to models trained on its outputs.

entry.title: The sudden collapse of the value of Chain-of-Thought (even summarized CoT) in the agentic era change...
entry.summary: Mollick argues that the collapse of chain-of-thought's value in the agentic era changes how we work with AI: effective steering now requires requesting interim outputs, tests, and using AI to troubleshoot issues.

entry.title: Our team got early access to Nemotron 3.5 Super VL a few weeks ago and decided to sprint a marathon’...
entry.summary: Ferenc Huszar describes his team's project using early access to NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: a new dataset of over 3,000 challenging Verus proofs of temporal logic (TLA+) properties, built to post-train a pre-release model for agentic software verification.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 15, 2026
entry.summary:
François Chollet sparked the sharpest debate, arguing that intelligence starved of sensory input hallucinates — citing string theory — and that autoregression alone cannot solve physical tasks, framing the embodied-AI moment perfectly.

  • Anthropic had a milestone day: reported $16.8B Q3 revenue with adjusted profitability (via Financial Times), shipped a major Claude Code desktop update for parallel sessions, opened OpenTelemetry tracing to public beta, and announced a Singapore office
entry.content:
François Chollet sparked the sharpest debate, arguing that intelligence starved of sensory input hallucinates — citing string theory — and that autoregression alone cannot solve physical tasks, framing the embodied-AI moment perfectly.

  • Anthropic had a milestone day: reported $16.8B Q3 revenue with adjusted profitability (via Financial Times), shipped a major Claude Code desktop update for parallel sessions, opened OpenTelemetry tracing to public beta, and announced a Singapore office

entry.title: String theory is what happens when an intelligent system is starved of sensory input and starts hall...
entry.summary: Chollet argues string theory exemplifies what happens when an intelligent system is starved of sensory input and begins hallucinating, concluding that intelligence requires grounding, that intelligence itself is rarely the bottleneck for solving impactful problems, and that the true bottleneck is iterated contact with reality.

entry.title:
Welcome to the era of embodied AI.
We are launching AA-Robotics v0.1, our research preview that mea...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches AA-Robotics v0.1, giving frontier LLMs in coding-agent harnesses direct control of a 6-axis robot arm across eight tasks testing dexterity and spatial reasoning. GPT-6 Astra places first ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5; models remain roughly two orders of magnitude slower and pricier than humans.

entry.title: SpaceXAI’s Grok Voice 3.0 is the new leading Speech to Speech model, debuting at #1 on the Artificia...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's flagship thread announces Grok Voice 3.0 as the new #1 speech-to-speech model on their index (86.9), up 5.6 points from Grok Voice 2.0, with details on pricing ($0.08/min via the SpaceXAI Realtime API), latency competitiveness, and sub-benchmark results including arena preference and task success.

entry.title: A conversation with Sergey Brin, @joshwoodward, @tulseedoshi, and @melvinjohnsonp about Gemini 4 Arg...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social coverage of the Gemini 4 Argon launch, Logan Kilpatrick shares a conversation with Sergey Brin, Josh Woodward, Tulsee Doshi, and Melvin Johnson discussing Gemini 4 Argon, how Google got here, and the roadmap ahead.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic's Q3 revenue was $16.8B, and the company is profitable on an adjusted ...
entry.summary: Brief report citing the Financial Times that Anthropic generated $16.8 billion in Q3 revenue and is profitable on an adjusted basis and cash-flow positive.

entry.title: TPUs have different bottlenecks from GPUs: few cores so you don’t need yo think about parallelism as...
entry.summary: Tri Dao explains that TPUs differ from GPUs in bottleneck structure: fewer cores reduce parallelism concerns, large VMEM makes kernel fusion easier, but vector units have lower throughput so non-matmul operations need much more care.

entry.title: We've been working hard on making the Claude Code desktop app great for running lots of sessions sid...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account announces a major Claude Code desktop app update focused on running many sessions side by side, with faster session starts and better visibility into each session's activity.

entry.title: Now in public beta, Claude Platform can send OpenTelemetry traces from the Messages API, Claude Mana...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces public beta support for OpenTelemetry tracing on the Claude Platform, covering the Messages API, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude SDKs, exportable to external observability stacks.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon is already unlocking new scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusio...
entry.summary: The anchor tweet of a DeepMind thread claiming Gemini 4 Argon is already driving scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and protein design, with links to specific case studies.

entry.title: We’ve added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to AA-AgentPerf, with results for NVIDIA and AMD hardware. At 100 to...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to its AA-AgentPerf agentic inference benchmark, reporting NVIDIA GB300 leading with up to 261M tokens/s per MW at 100 tokens/s per user. The benchmark replays real agentic coding sessions with prompt caching and tool-call delays, and the leaderboard now features four models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.2/5.3.

entry.title: after switching our approach to building a "FirmOS", I'm increasingly confident that the future of a...
entry.summary: Yohei Nakajima (BabyAGI creator) argues the future of human-agent collaboration in organizations is a 'CompanyOS' — a continuously updated operating system storing rules, processes, decisions, and tooling rather than a monolithic 'company brain'. He frames it as a 'flipped playbook': instead of writing rules first (waterfall-style), the playbook evolves daily as the business learns, with source-of-truth data remaining in existing tools like CRMs.

entry.title: Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This u...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas describes a user case where Perplexity Computer took a Windows-only mechanical keyboard app with no documentation, decompiled the binary with headless Ghidra in its cloud sandbox, and rebuilt it as a native Rust app for Linux with music-synced lighting, 3D view, remapping, macros, and profiles.

entry.title: We’ve opened an office in Singapore—our fifth in the Asia-Pacific region. We’ve also signed an MOU w...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and a memorandum of understanding with the Singaporean government covering AI safety and responsible adoption.

entry.title: The first clear sighting of a rogue agent fleet from China using open weights models. Like the OpenA...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights what he calls the first clear sighting of a rogue autonomous agent fleet from China using open weights models, apparently performing single-minded research tasks such as mapping popular park entrances in China, analogous to reported OpenAI swarms, calling it a harbinger of the future.

entry.title: Claude Code Desktop is now so much aware of its own capabilities and how it can work with you, like ...

entry.title: You can't solve real-world physical tasks through autoregressive sampling alone. The physical world ...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that real-world physical tasks cannot be solved by autoregressive sampling alone because the physical world punishes hallucination and approximate pattern matching; he contends autonomous robotics requires engineering causality and discrete reasoning into the loop, endorsing Biwei Huang and Aether AI's foundational work along these lines.
